title: Congruence from Transformation Sequences Review Test
description: Review transformation-sequence evidence for congruence and corresponding parts.

questions.questionText: Which transformation is rigid?
questions.explanation: A reflection preserves side lengths and angles.

questions.questionText: A triangle is translated and then rotated. What is true?
options: The final triangle has different angle measures.
The final triangle is similar but not congruent.
The final triangle is congruent to the original.
questions.correctAnswer: The final triangle is congruent to the original.
questions.explanation: Both moves are rigid.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC maps to triangle DEF. Which vertex corresponds to B?
questions.explanation: The second vertex maps to the second vertex.

questions.questionText: Which sequence is not fully rigid?
questions.explanation: The dilation changes size.

questions.questionText: What do rigid transformations preserve?
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape.

questions.questionText: If figure A is reflected to figure B, what may change?
questions.explanation: Reflection can flip orientation but remains rigid.

questions.questionText: Which evidence best proves congruence?
options: Both figures are on a grid.
A rigid sequence maps one figure exactly onto the other.
Both figures are near the origin.
questions.correctAnswer: A rigid sequence maps one figure exactly onto the other.
questions.explanation: An exact rigid mapping proves congruence.

questions.questionText: A dilation with scale factor 1 is included in a sequence. What happens to size?
questions.explanation: Scale factor 1 does not change lengths.

questions.questionText: Quadrilateral ABCD maps to WXYZ. Which side corresponds to BC?
questions.explanation: B maps to X and C maps to Y.

questions.questionText: A student says equal area proves congruence. Which response is best?
options: Equal area alone is not enough to prove congruence.
Equal area always means same side lengths.
questions.correctAnswer: Equal area alone is not enough to prove congruence.
questions.explanation: Different shapes can share the same area.

questions.questionText: A figure is rotated, translated, and stretched. What is the best conclusion?
options: The final figure must be congruent.
The stretch makes it more congruent.
The translation changes all angle measures.
The final figure is not guaranteed congruent.
questions.correctAnswer: The final figure is not guaranteed congruent.
questions.explanation: A stretch is not rigid.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle LMN. Which angle corresponds to angle C?
questions.explanation: C is third, so it corresponds to N.

questions.questionText: A segment is mapped by a reflection and translation. If the original length is 13, what is the image length?
questions.explanation: Rigid moves preserve length.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly uses transformation evidence?
options: The figures are congruent because a reflection and rotation map one onto the other.
The figures are congruent because they look close.
The figures are congruent because one is higher.
The figures are congruent because both names have three letters.
questions.correctAnswer: The figures are congruent because a reflection and rotation map one onto the other.
questions.explanation: Reflection and rotation are rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: A sequence maps triangle PQR to triangle STU. Which side corresponds to PR?
questions.explanation: P maps to S and R maps to U.

questions.questionText: Which property can change during a rigid transformation sequence?
questions.explanation: The figure can move, but its measurements stay the same.

questions.questionText: Which sequence could map congruent figures?
questions.explanation: The first sequence uses only rigid moves.

questions.questionText: A reflection reverses clockwise order. Does that prevent congruence?
options: Yes, orientation must stay the same.
No, orientation may reverse while lengths and angles stay the same.
questions.correctAnswer: No, orientation may reverse while lengths and angles stay the same.
questions.explanation: Reflections are rigid even though orientation changes.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC maps to DEF by rigid transformations. If angle A is 72 degrees, what is angle D?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal.

questions.questionText: What is wrong with a congruence proof that includes a dilation by 1/2?
options: The dilation changes only the labels.
The dilation preserves congruence like a rotation.
The dilation keeps every distance fixed.
questions.explanation: A scale factor other than 1 changes size.
